question: Iran full airspace closure by July 31?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran initiates a general closure of its airspace, that is not solely due to weather conditions, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “general closure” refers to a cancellation or suspension of aviation which is generally applicable to all commercial flights transiting Iranian airspace (“Tehran FIR”). A qualifying closure must apply generally to all of Iran or the Tehran FIR; limited cancellations, delays, or partial closures will not qualify. A closure which applies generally to commercial aviation across Iranian airspace, with limited exceptions for certain categories of flights, however, will qualify (e.g. exceptions for certain flights pre-approved by the Iranian Civil Aviation Authority may be permitted).

Qualifying previous examples include the February 28, 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace (https://www.iranintl.com/en/202602289115) and the January 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace except to international flights with express governmental permission (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-shuts-airspace-most-flights-flightradar24-says-2026-01-14/). Non-qualifying examples include the January 27, 2026 partial closure of Iranian airspace around the Strait of Hormuz (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-issues-airspace-notice-for-military-drills-near-strait-of-hormuz/3812508), the April 2024 closure of Iran’s western airspace (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-airports-cancel-flights-until-monday-morning-2024-04-14/), and the January 25 - April 25, 2026 VFR (Visual Flight Rules) flights suspension which did not broadly close commercial aviation in Iran (https://www.intellinews.com/iran-suspends-general-aviation-and-vfr-flights-in-new-airspace-directive-421997/).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Iran will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions, earthquakes, or volcanic eruptions, will not qualify.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Iranian aviation authorities and a consensus of credible reporting.
research:
I found no report of a full, Iran-ordered closure of the Tehran FIR between the market's creation (2026-06-25) and 2026-07-20. I left out everything published after 2026-07-20. Many direct page fetches (Polymarket, EASA, Orrery, Lines) were blocked by the proxy, so most of the points below come from search-result summaries.

## 1. Resolution source
- The rules use official statements from Iran's aviation authorities (Civil Aviation Organization and NOTAMs) plus a consensus of credible reporting. There is no single data series. The Polymarket event page wouldn't load. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/iran-full-airspace-closure-byptptpt-20260625195253028)
- 2026-06-25: the event was created then. The ID in its URL contains "20260625", so the June 8 closure doesn't count for this market. [Lines](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/world/iran-full-airspace-closure-byptptpt-20260625195253028)
- I couldn't get the text of the Iranian NOTAM in force on July 20.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing so far settles the question. I found no report of a nationwide closure or suspension of all commercial flights between June 25 and July 20.
- 2026-07-08: EASA issued CZIB-2026-04, advising airlines to avoid the Tehran FIR at all altitudes. This is a foreign advisory, so it doesn't count. [EASA](https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/air-operations/czibs/czib-2026-04)
- Around 2026-07-12: Iranian media reported that all airports in Hormozgan province were closed until further notice. That is a regional closure, so it doesn't count. [Liveuamap](https://iran.liveuamap.com/en/2026/8-july-12-iranian-media-all-airports-in-hormozgan-province), [MENAFN](https://menafn.com/1111372899/Iran-Closes-Hormozgan-Airports-Amid-Security-Concerns)
- Undated: Mehr reportedly later said the Hormozgan airports were still operating. [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/iran-denies-hormozgan-airport-shutdown-amid-post-conflict-recovery/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-07-20: Reuters reported that mediators had sent Iran a proposal for a 10-day ceasefire. It was not clear whether Tehran had accepted. [1lurer/Reuters](https://www.1lurer.am/en/2026/07/20/Mediators-propose-10-day-ceasefire-in-Iran-US-conflict-Reuters/1548244)
- 2026-07-18: Iran said it was suspending its commitments under the Islamabad MoU. About 50 people had been killed in US strikes in July. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/18/iran-accuses-us-of-striking-critical-infrastructure-as-war-intensifies), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/18/world/live-news/iran-war-trump)
- 2026-07-17: US strikes hit bridges in Hormozgan, electrical infrastructure and Iranshahr airport. [Newscord](https://newscord.org/article/us-strikes-iran-bridges-for-seventh-night-killing-at-least-seven-in-hormozgan--Story_20260717_UShitsbridgesandener2f092a26)
- 2026-07-12: a large US wave of strikes followed Iran closing the Strait of Hormuz. [Archypedia](https://archypedia.news/news/us-strikes-iran-hormuz-closure/)
- 2026-07-07 to 07-08: Trump called the MoU "over" and the ceasefire collapsed. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire)
- 2026-06-17: a US-Iran memorandum extended the truce by 60 days. [EASA](https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/air-operations/czibs/czib-2026-04)

## 4. Base rates
I found these Iran-ordered general closures in 2026:
- 2026-01-14: closed to most flights for a few hours. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/15/iran-briefly-closes-airspace-as-us-tensions-rise-flights-rerouted-across-region.html)
- 2026-02-28: whole country closed, lasting into March/April. Flights at IKA resumed 2026-04-25. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/4/25/iran-resumes-commercial-flights-from-tehran-airport)
- 2026-06-08: western airspace closed, then all flights cancelled nationwide (Mashhad stayed open for Hajj returns). The airspace reopened soon after. [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20260608/21ed929d1a834302bf894b327182f078/c.html), [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202606085568), [WANA](https://wanaen.com/civil-aviation-organization-reopens-iranian-airspace/)

That is roughly 3 in about 6.5 months, each tied to the start of strikes or a sharp jump in tension. The current US strike campaign has run since about July 8, and no full closure has followed in roughly 12 days. Iran instead seems to be closing airports one region at a time.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-06-26: Lines showed July 31 at 24% Yes (about $627K volume) and August 31 at 36%. [Lines](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/world/iran-full-airspace-closure-byptptpt-20260625195253028)
- Undated snapshots of July 31 show 34.5% (up from 28%), 21.5% (after Mehr said the Hormozgan airports were operating) and 5¢ on an Orrery cluster page. I couldn't tell when each was taken. [Orrery move](https://orrery.me/share/move/iran-closes-its-airspace-by-july-31-478), [Orrery event](https://orrery.me/events/iran-full-airspace-closure-byptptpt-20260625195253028), [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/iran-denies-hormozgan-airport-shutdown-amid-post-conflict-recovery/)
- 2026-07-19: a snapshot reportedly showed August 31 at 50% Yes. [Orrery](https://orrery.me/markets/iran-full-airspace-closure-by-august-31-20260625195254151-668)
- I found no Kalshi, Manifold or expert forecasts.

## 6. Upcoming events before July 31
- Whether Iran accepts the proposed 10-day ceasefire (reported 2026-07-20).
- Whether US strikes continue or intensify, especially on Tehran or air-defense targets. Earlier full closures came right at the start of large waves of strikes.
- Iran's response to the US troop deaths, such as missile salvos that could prompt a precautionary closure.
- New NOTAMs from Iran's CAO. Their spokesperson, Majid Akhavan, has made the announcements in past episodes.
- The EASA advisory runs until July 31, but foreign advisories don't count toward resolution.
